home:
webCLI

Twelve tools that each transform one kind of thing in a browser tab. What you give one is not uploaded, with two stated exceptions below; the paper explains the architecture. Each is listed with what goes in, what comes out, what it is not, and a state that says how far to trust it.

Video and audio

ffmpeg

In: a video, audio or image file from your device. Out: that media trimmed, converted, scaled or compressed, or as a GIF or extracted audio. Not: hls, which only builds and manages adaptive-streaming libraries; this one is the general transforms.

early. No gate table yet and no run= surface.

hls

In: an MP4 and the git repository it should live in. Out: a versioned adaptive-streaming release (ladder, segments, playlists) committed and tagged name/vN. Not: ffmpeg, which does general transforms and keeps nothing; this one does exactly one thing.

working. Its gates pass. Publishing is a commit to your repository, so it is egress, and it is yours to start. H.264 only; variable-frame-rate and rotated files are refused by name.

whisper

In: an audio or video file from your device. Out: a transcript as text, SRT or WebVTT. Not: dub, which goes the other way, from subtitles to speech.

early. No gate table yet and no run= surface. The Whisper model is downloaded on first use.

dub

In: an SRT file. Out: one WAV with every cue spoken at its timestamp, and a report.json of overruns and collisions. Not: whisper, which turns speech into text; this only writes speech, and never time-stretches a cue.

working. Its gates pass. Byte-identical output holds on the wasm device with q8, not on webgpu. No run= surface yet.

3D and motion

3mf

In: a GLB model. Out: a 3MF with its materials segmented by colour, for multi-material printing. Not: rig, which bakes motion into an animated GLB; this converts one model to one print format and animates nothing.

early. GLB in, 3MF out, nothing else. No gate table yet and no run= surface.

mocap

In: a webcam or a video file of a person. Out: body motion as a BVH and face motion as ARKit blendshapes JSON. Not: rig, which retargets motion onto a character you bring; this one only records, and bakes only onto its two bundled avatars.

early. The source repository is private, so there is no open licence yet. One webcam cannot give studio-grade face and body at once. First load is about 100 MB.

rig

In: a skinned character (FBX, GLB or VRM) and motion files (BVH, FBX or GLB). Out: one optimized animated GLB carrying each motion as its own track. Not: mocap, which records motion from a camera; this one watches nothing and retargets motion that already exists.

early. The optional in-page assist is off by default; turning it on downloads about 1 GB of model weights. Its tests are not yet published as a gate table.

Images

magick

In: image files from your device. Out: those images converted between 100+ formats, or edited with chained, batchable operations. Not: look, which edits the textures and materials of a VRM avatar; this one edits pictures and knows nothing of avatars.

early. No gate table yet and no run= surface.

look

In: a VRM avatar. Out: the same avatar, as a VRM, with its textures, materials, outfits or accessories changed. Not: portrait, which reads a face from a photo and binds it to a VRM; this one never sees a photo.

early. The editor re-exports through its own writer, so the output is not a byte-audited edit of the input. Determinism is measured on the two bundled bases only.

portrait

In: a photo of one face and a base VRM. Out: that VRM with its expressions bound to the face read from the photo. Not: look, which edits an avatar's textures and outfits by hand; this one reads a face, and its result is not a likeness.

early. Approximate, not a likeness. One clear front-facing face. The photo is read from a local file only, so a run needs a person or a runner with the file.

Text and publishing

blog

In: markdown posts in a GitHub repository. Out: static HTML pages, a feed and a sitemap committed back to that repository. Not: hls, which makes the video releases a post can embed; this one encodes no video.

early. Publishing is a commit to your repository, so it is egress, and it is yours to start. Its own test suite had 5 failures of 598 on 2026-11-15. Every page it generates loads Font Awesome from cdnjs, with no way to turn that off.

chat

In: text you type. Out: a reply from a language model running on your own GPU. Not: blog, which writes to a repository and publishes; this one keeps conversations in this browser and sends them nowhere.

early. Needs WebGPU. Model weights are downloaded on first use. Conversations are saved in this browser's localStorage. No gate table yet.

What all twelve share

Stated once here, so it cannot drift across twelve READMEs. The left column is the claim; the right is what has been measured, and where nothing has been measured it says so.

ClaimMeasured today
A persistent egress ledger that reads zero12 of 12 made no non-GET request, sent no request body and made no request after the network was cut, from load to idle (2026-11-16). A representative operation is written for 0 of 12.
connect-src 'none' once loaded0 of 12. 4 ship a Content-Security-Policy at all.
No credentials reachable from a workerNot measured.
Refusals by name rather than silent approximationNot measured across the family.
An open licence11 of 12; the source of mocap is not public yet.
Operates offline once loadedNot measured.

Two exceptions, and they are part of the claim. Loading is egress: fetching the WebAssembly core and any model is a request, always a GET with no body, and each tool's fetches in tools.json names what it fetches. Publishing is egress the user starts: hls and blog commit to a repository, and nothing is sent until you press Publish; hls says so in its Privacy and Egress section.

The ledger, per tool

Each tool's origin was loaded in a fresh Chrome profile with the cache off, left idle for 8 s, then the network was cut and it was left idle for 5 s more; every request was logged from the DevTools protocol. Hosts other than the tool's own are what it fetched while loading, the first exception above. Non-GET and body bytes count anything that is not a bodiless GET. No tool was operated (that is 0 of 12 representative operations written), so this is load and idle, not use.

Measured on this page

This page makes no request to any other host; CI loads it with a cold cache and fails on the first request that is not to its own origin, and the same check can be repeated in DevTools, Network, with Disable cache on.

Lab measurement of this page, median of 5: 0 JavaScript files, 2 requests, 92.4 KB transferred, first contentful paint 584 ms, largest contentful paint 616 ms, total blocking time 0 ms.

Method: blog-webCLI's cli/speed.mjs in headless Chrome: Slow 4G (1.6 Mbit/s down, 150 ms round trip), 4x CPU slowdown, a 390 px phone, a new browser profile for every run with the cache off, 5 runs, median reported; FCP and LCP from PerformanceObserver, total blocking time summed from long tasks after first paint; JavaScript counted from the network log. Lab data from one machine, served from 127.0.0.1, so the throttle supplies the latency but not DNS, TLS or distance; measured 2026-11-16.

Agents and scripts

The tools are meant to be driven by a URL and to return an artifact; 3 of 12 (rig, look, portrait) have the run= surface today. tools.json is the machine-readable index of this page: for each tool its origin, what it fetches and, where it has one, that surface (parameters, window.__webcli_result, test ids). Nothing here needs an account; the two tools that publish are the exception stated above.

  • portrait privacy audit (zero egress)
  • rig: how to verify zero egress, asserted by its test suite
